mechanism_narrative: The four-week decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects weaker weekday trip generation; that suppresses incidental shopping and dining visits, so RETAIL_REC will stay lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not below its last-28-day mean, despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining depressed or declining further.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM falls sharply toward baseline, routine errand traffic shifts from one-stop essential trips to discretionary trips, raising retail-and-recreation mobility within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 10 points above baseline after being above 20 points in the prior two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks after GROCERY_PHARM drops below the stated threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous slump in PARKS and WORKPLACES indicates broad reductions in both leisure and commute traffic, which weakens out-of-home exposure and pulls RETAIL_REC down over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though both PARKS and WORKPLACES remain below their recent averages.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while TRANSIT stays suppressed, people substitute home-based activity for shopping trips, so retail-and-recreation mobility declines further within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 20 points while TRANSIT stays below -30 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall after the stated residential-transit regime holds for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after a deep weekly trough signals improving outdoor activity and generally higher local circulation, which spills into retail visits with about a one-week lag.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points week-on-week after being below -40 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week after PARKS rebounds by at least 10 points from a sub -40 level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates more commuting and cross-district movement; that increases exposure to retail corridors and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 28 days while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both trend upward.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM is elevated but stable, households complete essential shopping without increasing discretionary trips, so retail mobility does not recover and stays below the prior four-week average.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains between 0 and 15 points for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean within two weeks while GROCERY_PHARM remains in the stated band.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL eases while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stop falling, mobility is rotating back toward outside-the-home activity, and RETAIL_REC should improve over the next month.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 2 points while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each rise week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-28-day mean after residential mobility eases and transit/workplace mobility turns up.
